Let the lower triangular base be \(ABC\), with \(A\) the front vertex, and let \(A'\) be the corresponding top vertex above \(A\). The cut plane passes through \(A'\) and the midpoints \(M,N\) of \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{AC}\).

The part containing \(A\) is the tetrahedron \(A A' M N\). Since \(M,N\) are midpoints,
\[
[AMN]=\frac14[ABC].
\]
The perpendicular distance from \(A'\) to the base plane equals the height \(h\) of the prism. Thus
\[
V_{\text{tetra}}
=\frac13[AMN]h
=\frac13\cdot \frac14[ABC]\cdot h
=\frac1{12}\bigl([ABC]h\bigr).
\]
But \([ABC]h\) is the full prism volume, \(504\). Therefore the desired volume is
\[
\frac{504}{12}=42.
\]

\[
